one_liner: Tiny header-only C++20 SPSC ring-buffer logger; about 5.3x spdlog async throughput to /dev/null on an Apple M3.
what_it_does: A single 188-line header that gives one application thread a LOG(logger, "fmt {}", args...) macro writing into a fixed in-object ring of Capacity slots of MaxMsgLen bytes (defaults 8192 x 256); a background thread drains the ring to a caller-owned FILE*. Format strings are template arguments, so a placeholder/argument count mismatch is a compile error. It is not an spdlog replacement: there are no levels, timestamps, sinks, patterns or multi-thread producers, and log() returns false (drops) when the ring is full.
how_it_is_fast: Classic Lamport SPSC queue: monotonic 64-bit head and tail indices, each with a single writer, published with release stores and read with acquire loads, so no mutex or CAS; the two indices are alignas(128) to avoid false sharing. The producer formats in place into the slot with std::to_chars and memcpy (no heap, no locale), and the consumer coalesces every pending slot into a 64 KiB stack buffer written with one fwrite per pass. spdlog async, by contrast, formats into a heap-backed message, pushes through a mutex-guarded MPMC queue and writes through a mutex sink.
when_to_use: Exactly one hot thread emitting short integer/C-string log lines where the enqueue cost must stay in the tens of nanoseconds.
Learning or teaching material for an acquire/release SPSC ring with compile-time format checking.
A starting point to vendor and extend inside your own code base, once the author adds a license.
Workloads that tolerate dropped lines under bursts (the producer never blocks).
when_not_to_use: Multiple producer threads: it is SPSC only, and calling log() from two threads is a data race.
Anything needing floats, std::string, std::string_view, bool, user types, levels, timestamps or rotation: emit_arg only handles integral types and const char*.
Production use or redistribution: the repo has no license file, 0 stars and 3 commits.
Battery- or CPU-constrained systems: the consumer spins with std::this_thread::yield() whenever the ring is empty.
Thread stacks smaller than a few MB: the whole ring lives inside the Logger object (about 2.1 MB at the defaults), so a stack-allocated Logger can overflow.

integration.min_toolchain: C++20 (class-type NTTPs, consteval); README builds with clang++ -std=c++20 -O2
integration.platforms: any with std::thread and a FILE* sink; measured on Apple M3 macOS and Intel Xeon Gold 6348 Linux
integration.thread_safety: one producer thread and the internal consumer thread only

gotchas: On a full ring log() drops and increments dropped(); the benchmark spins on log() until it succeeds, so its dropped() figure counts retries, not lost lines.

Integer truncation bug: when std::to_chars does not fit, it returns ptr == end with the range in an unspecified state, but emit_arg advances to res.ptr (the comment says it returns p), so truncated lines can contain garbage bytes.
No fflush: output reaches the FILE* buffer only; you must fflush/fclose the sink yourself after the Logger is destroyed. {{ escapes are not supported and extra {} pairs are treated as placeholders.
The README cites a 5M-message SPSC hash correctness test, but no test file is in the repository (only bench/ and examples/).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Only when you want a minimal, dependency-free SPSC enqueue you can read in one sitting; Quill, fmtlog, PlatformLab NanoLog and XTR are mature, multi-producer, licensed, and measured at single-digit ns per call in independent harnesses, so they are the default choices for real logging.
verified_claims_summary: bench/benchmark.cpp logs 5M "log line {} value={}" messages to /dev/null on an Apple M3 with clang++ -std=c++20 -O2: about 28M msg/s for this logger (spinning on a full 8192-slot, 128-byte ring) versus about 5M msg/s for spdlog create_async with basic_file_sink_mt, an 8192-entry blocking queue and one worker (5.3x); spdlog is the prebuilt Homebrew build and the timer stops before either queue is fully drained (at most 8192 messages each). The ~50M msg/s Xeon Gold 6348 figure has no spdlog row and no compiler stated.
status_note: Active but brand new (3 commits, last 2026-09-22, 0 stars) and unlicensed, so reference only; small enough to rewrite from the README's design notes.
